candidates.source_name: NBS – Pravidlá platobného systému SIPS (SIPS payment system rules)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative rules of the Slovak domestic interbank payment system SIPS/EURO SIPS operated by NBS: participation contract, message formats, operating timetable (časový harmonogram) and fee schedule (sadzobník). Changes here are binding operational deadlines for every SK participant.
candidates.source_subtype: central bank payment system rulebook page
candidates.suggested_collection_method: scheduled HTML diff of the rules page plus download/version-diff of linked PDFs (zmluva, harmonogram, sadzobník)
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on SIPS rules, then snowball into NBS payments section
queries_used: SIPS platobný systém NBS pravidlá prevádzky

candidates.source_name: NBS – Platobné systémy / TARGET Services (T2, T2S, TIPS) section
candidates.why_relevant: NBS pages on T2/T2S consolidation, TARGET-SK and TIPS describe Slovak participation conditions, DCA/TIPS account rules and migration milestones for SK banks and (since Oct 2025) non-bank PSPs.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: crawl section tree; track linked NBS decisions (rozhodnutia) as PDFs
queries_used: NBS TARGET T2 TIPS účastníci Slovensko platobné systémy dohľad

candidates.source_name: NBS decisions/rozhodnutia on payment system participation (e.g. rozhodnutie NBS č. 10/2022, 9/2018, 4/2010)
candidates.why_relevant: NBS decisions are the legally binding instrument setting harmonised participation conditions for TARGET2-SK/TARGET-SK, TIPS DCAs and ancillary-system settlement — the hard rule layer beneath the descriptive web pages.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: monitor NBS legal-acts listing (vestník / právne predpisy NBS) and fetch PDFs; also cross-check in Slov-Lex
queries_used: NBS TARGET T2 TIPS účastníci Slovensko platobné systémy dohľad

candidates.source_name: NBS – Inštitúcie elektronických peňazí (e-money institutions supervision & register)
candidates.why_relevant: NBS supervises and maintains the list of Slovak EMIs; the section carries licensing conditions and the authoritative national register — the entry gate for e-money business in SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: periodic snapshot of the register listing (entity add/remove diffing)
queries_used: NBS platobná inštitúcia inštitúcia elektronických peňazí povolenie licencia

candidates.source_name: NBS – Platobné inštitúcie a AISP: postup podania žiadosti / pred podaním žiadosti
candidates.why_relevant: Procedural rules for PI/PISP authorisation and AISP registration in SK, including the pre-application channel (psd2@nbs.sk) and the requirement of SK head office. Directly governs market entry conditions for payment providers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML change monitoring; capture linked application guidance PDFs
queries_used: NBS platobná inštitúcia inštitúcia elektronických peňazí povolenie licencia

candidates.source_name: NBS – Príručka pre prípravu žiadosti o udelenie povolenia (licensing application handbook, PDF)
candidates.why_relevant: Detailed NBS expectations for PI/EMI licence files (business model, capital, governance, outsourcing). Useful as a proxy for supervisory priorities and for benchmarking entry effort.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PDF version tracking (hash + date)
queries_used: NBS platobná inštitúcia inštitúcia elektronických peňazí povolenie licencia

candidates.source_name: NBS – Okamžité platby a overenie prijímateľa (instant payments & VOP hub)
candidates.why_relevant: NBS's national explainer/tracker for IPR (EU 2024/886) obligations: receive from 9 Jan 2025, send + free Verification of Payee from 9 Oct 2025. The canonical SK-language statement of these deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: page monitoring + NBS aktuality RSS/news scraping

candidates.source_name: NBS aktuality – news on opening SIPS/TARGET-SK to non-bank PSPs
candidates.why_relevant: Announces that from 6 Oct 2025 PIs and EMIs may apply to participate directly in SIPS or TARGET-SK — a structural change in SK payment-market access, and a leading indicator of new direct participants.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: monitor nbs.sk/aktuality feed filtered on payments keywords

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council – SCT Inst rulebook & implementation guidelines
candidates.why_relevant: The scheme rulebook that binds SK PSPs contractually rather than by national law: 2025 SCT Inst v1.1 in force to 21 Nov 2027, 5/7/9-second timing rules, structured-address migration (Nov 2026). These deadlines never appear in Slovak legislation.
candidates.legal_status: scheme body publication; check reuse terms for redistribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: track document-library listing pages for new rulebook versions/change requests; store PDFs
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search on rulebook migration deadlines
queries_used: EPC SEPA rulebook 2027 SCT Inst migration deadline payment service providers

candidates.source_name: European Payments Council – Verification of Payee (VOP) scheme rulebook & EPC Directory Service
candidates.why_relevant: VOP rulebook in force since 5 Oct 2025; all SCT/SCT Inst participants must adhere and fund the EDS for an initial 3 years. Directly determines SK PSP obligations and vendor (RVM) demand.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: version-diff rulebook PDFs (v1.0 2024 vs v1.1 2026) and monitor VOP news/FAQ pages
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search + snowball into EPC FAQ/document library
queries_used: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook register of participants SEPA scheme adherence

candidates.source_name: EPC Register of Participants (SEPA scheme adherence lists)
candidates.why_relevant: Adherence registers show which SK PSPs (and which RVMs serving them) are live in SCT, SCT Inst and VOP — the best objective indicator of Slovak scheme readiness and of vendor footprints.
candidates.access_status: public (register may be behind a separate search app)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: download the register export filtered on country=SK; snapshot monthly
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search referencing register counts (2,673 PSPs, 55 RVMs)
queries_used: EPC Verification of Payee scheme rulebook register of participants SEPA scheme adherence

candidates.source_name: EBA central register of payment and electronic money institutions (PSD2)
candidates.why_relevant: EU-wide, daily-updated, downloadable register fed by NBS. Gives a machine-readable view of SK PIs/EMIs/PISPs/AISPs plus inbound passporting into Slovakia — better for time-series than the NBS HTML lists.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: scheduled bulk download, filter home country = SK plus passporting-in rows; diff monthly

candidates.why_relevant: The national statute governing payment services, PI/EMI licensing and payment systems in SK (transposing PSD2; future home of PSD3/PSR alignment). Slov-Lex gives consolidated versions and effective dates.

negative_findings.description: No public, standalone NBS 'payment systems oversight report' (dohľad nad platobnými systémami) page was identified in this pass; oversight content appears embedded in NBS annual reports (výročná správa) chapters on platobný styk.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only older annual-report PDF chapters surfaced (vs2003/vs2004 kapitola Platobný styk); no current standalone oversight publication found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Oversight assessments of SIPS/card schemes are a key credibility anchor; if they exist only inside annual reports, collection must target report chapters, not a page.

negative_findings.description: Card scheme mandate calendars for Europe (Mastercard release bulletins, Visa Business News) are member-gated; only consolidated public rulebooks and third-party vendor digests are openly reachable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public Visa rules PDF found; Mastercard bulletins require Mastercard Connect credentials.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme mandate deadlines are exactly the cell's stated blind spot; without member access the intelligence must be reconstructed from vendor commentary with lower confidence.

negative_findings.description: 'SIPS' is ambiguous: it denotes both the Slovak interbank system (Slovak Interbank Payment System / EURO SIPS) and the ECB Regulation on Systemically Important Payment Systems.
negative_findings.result_summary: A single SK query returned both NBS SIPS pages and an EUR-Lex SIPS Regulation summary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on 'SIPS' will produce false positives; queries must be disambiguated with 'platobný systém SIPS' + 'NBS'.

negative_findings.description: No established Slovak-language term was found for scheme-level artefacts such as 'scheme rulebook' or 'Routing and Verification Mechanism (RVM)'; SK material uses descriptive phrasing or the English terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: SK searches on scheme rulebooks returned EU/EN sources or generic 'pravidlá schémy' phrasing only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-rulebook monitoring for SK cannot rely on Slovak keywords; it must be done in English at EPC/scheme level and then mapped to SK participants.

negative_findings.description: No page was fetched in this pass; all URLs come from search-result metadata and are unverified for liveness. The Mastercard rules landing URL in particular is a well-known address that was not confirmed by a fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search-only discovery; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification should expect some redirects, especially on nbs.sk (site was restructured from www.nbs.sk/_img/... to nbs.sk/...) and nrsr.sk DocID links.

coverage_gaps.description: SK card processing and ATM/POS infrastructure operators (e.g. the ancillary systems settling in TARGET-SK such as the card clearing operator, and CDCP SR) were only surfaced indirectly via NBS text; no dedicated operator sources were profiled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball the NBS list of ancillary systems (prídavné/pridružené systémy) and profile each operator's own rules/tariff pages.

coverage_gaps.description: No NBS-run public consultation channel for payments (as distinct from MF SR legislative consultation) was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check nbs.sk for 'konzultácie'/'metodické usmernenia'/'opatrenia NBS' sections and the NBS Vestník for payments-related instruments.

coverage_gaps.description: E-money/PI prudential reporting and statistical outputs (NBS payment statistics under ECB Regulation 2020/2011) were not covered in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add NBS statistics portal (štatistika platobného styku) and ECB Payments Statistics as quantitative complements to the rule-layer sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Scheme-rulebook layer (EPC, Visa, Mastercard) is English-only; there is no Slovak-language early-warning channel for scheme deadlines other than SBA and press coverage after the fact.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair EN scheme monitoring with SK-language SBA/bank monitoring to detect lag between rulebook publication and SK implementation.

brief: For Slovak payments infrastructure and scheme rules the landscape splits cleanly into three layers. The national layer is dominated by NBS, which is simultaneously operator (SIPS/EURO SIPS, TARGET-SK, TIPS), rule-setter (rozhodnutia NBS, participation contracts, harmonogram and sadzobník) and licensor/supervisor of platobné inštitúcie and inštitúcie elektronických peňazí, with Slov-Lex, NR SR and EUR-Lex carrying the binding statutory texts in Slovak. The scheme layer that actually imposes migration deadlines on SK PSPs sits outside national law and outside Slovak: the EPC rulebooks (SCT, SCT Inst 2025 v1.1 in force to Nov 2027, VOP in force since Oct 2025 with mandatory adherence) and the card schemes, where Visa publishes a dated public rulebook but Mastercard's mandate bulletins are member-gated — the main access blocker in this cell. Corroboration of actual implementation comes from the Slovak Banking Association, individual bank payment/T&C pages and business press, which are the only Slovak-language sources that reflect scheme deadlines at all.
